title: Mysore Masala Dosa

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric, green chillies

recipe: Prepare or use fermented dosa batter of pouring consistency.
For filling: Boil and mash potatoes. Temper mustard, curry leaves, green chillies and onion; add turmeric and salt. Mix with potatoes.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin circle. Drizzle oil/ghee. Spread a thin layer of red chilli-garlic chutney on the inner surface.
Place potato filling in the centre, fold the dosa and roast till crisp and golden.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
tips: The distinctive red chutney inside distinguishes Mysore Masala Dosa from regular masala dosa.
Crispy exterior and soft potato filling are key.

title: Thatte Idli
recipe: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 4–6 hours. Grind to a smooth, slightly coarse batter. Ferment overnight.
Grease large flat idli plates (thatte plates). Pour batter to fill the plates.
Steam for 12–15 minutes till a toothpick comes out clean.
Serve soft, large thatte idlis with coconut chutney, sambar or potato sagu.
tips: Thatte means plate – these are larger and flatter than regular idlis.
Popular in Bengaluru and surrounding areas; very soft texture.

title: Akki Rotti

ingredients.name: Onion, carrot, dill leaves or coriander

recipe: Mix rice flour with finely chopped onion, grated carrot, dill/coriander, green chillies, cumin, curry leaves, salt and enough hot water to form a soft dough.
Take a portion, pat it thin on a banana leaf, plastic sheet or directly on a hot greased tawa (make a small hole in the centre if desired).
Drizzle oil and cook on both sides till golden spots appear and edges crisp.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or any spicy curry.
tips: Pat the rotti thin for crispiness.
A traditional breakfast from South Karnataka and coastal regions.

title: Neer Dosa
recipe: Soak rice for 3–4 hours. Grind with coconut (if using) and water to a very thin, watery batter. Add salt.
Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned tawa. Pour a ladle of batter and swirl quickly to form a thin lace-like dosa. Do not spread with a ladle.
Cover and cook for 1–2 minutes till the surface sets (no need to flip).
Fold into triangle or roll and serve with coconut chutney, chicken curry or vegetable stew.
tips: Neer means water – the batter is intentionally very thin.
Coastal Karnataka (Mangaluru / Malenadu) specialty; soft and delicate.

title: Bisi Bele Bath

ingredients.name: Bisi bele bath powder / spice mix

recipe: Pressure-cook rice, toor dal and vegetables together with turmeric and water till soft.
Extract tamarind pulp. In a pan heat ghee, temper mustard, curry leaves and cashews. Add the cooked mixture, bisi bele bath powder, tamarind, jaggery and salt.
Simmer, adding water to reach a porridge-like consistency. Mash lightly if desired.
Serve piping hot with a generous dollop of ghee, potato chips or boondi and raita.
tips: The name means ‘hot lentil rice’. Origin linked to Mysore royal kitchens.
Consistency should be soft and slightly runny – not dry.

title: Ragi Mudde
recipe: Bring water with a pinch of salt to a rolling boil.
Lower heat and gradually add ragi flour while stirring vigorously with a wooden stick (mudde kolu) to avoid lumps.
Cook on low heat, continuing to stir and press, until the mixture becomes a soft, non-sticky dough that leaves the sides of the pan.
Wet hands and shape into smooth round balls (mudde).
Serve hot with bassaru, upsaaru, sambar or any spicy curry. Traditionally swallowed in small portions without chewing.
tips: Continuous stirring is essential for smooth texture.
A nutritious staple of rural South Karnataka, especially Mandya and Mysuru regions.

title: Chitranna (Lemon Rice)

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, curry leaves

recipe: Heat oil, temper mustard, urad dal, chana dal, peanuts, curry leaves, green chillies and asafoetida.
Add turmeric and the cooked rice. Mix gently.
Switch off heat, add lemon juice, salt and chopped coriander. Mix well.
Serve with papad, yogurt or any side dish.
tips: Use cooled leftover rice for best texture.
A simple, tangy rice dish common in everyday Karnataka meals and festivals.

title: Holige / Obbattu
recipe: Cook dal till soft, drain and mash. Cook with jaggery till thick. Add cardamom. Cool to form the stuffing (holige filling).
Knead a soft dough with flour, a pinch of turmeric, salt, oil and water. Rest.
Stuff portions of dough with the sweet filling, seal and roll carefully into thin rounds.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides till golden.
Serve warm with ghee or milk.
tips: Also called Obbattu. A must for festivals like Ugadi and weddings.
Coconut-jaggery version is also popular.

title: Kori Gassi (Mangalorean Chicken Curry)

ingredients.name: Tamarind, chilli powder, coriander, turmeric, fenugreek

recipe: Dry-roast grated coconut with spices (coriander, chilli, fenugreek etc.) and grind to a smooth paste with a little water.
Sauté onion, ginger-garlic and curry leaves. Add chicken and sear.
Add the coconut masala, tamarind extract, salt and water. Simmer till chicken is cooked and gravy thickens.
Serve with neer dosa, kori rotti or rice.
tips: Classic Mangalorean / coastal Karnataka chicken curry.
The roasted coconut base gives it a distinctive flavour.

title: Maddur Vada

ingredients.name: Green chillies, curry leaves, cumin, sesame

recipe: Mix rice flour, maida, rava, finely chopped onion, green chillies, curry leaves, cumin, sesame and salt.
Add water little by little to form a stiff dough.
Pinch small portions, flatten into thin discs with a hole or plain round shape.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil till crisp and golden.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or as is with tea.
tips: Originates from the town of Maddur in Karnataka.
Crispy outside, slightly soft inside – perfect tea-time snack.

title: Goli Baje (Mangalore Bajji)

ingredients.name: Green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, coriander

recipe: Mix maida, curd, finely chopped green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, coriander, salt and a pinch of soda into a thick batter. Rest 15–20 minutes.
Heat oil. Drop small spoonfuls of batter and deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
Drain and serve hot with coconut chutney.
tips: Also called Mangalore Bajji. Soft and spongy texture is characteristic.
Best eaten fresh.

title: Rava Idli

ingredients.name: Mustard, chana dal, urad dal, curry leaves, cashews

recipe: Dry-roast rava lightly. Temper mustard, dals, curry leaves, cashews, green chillies and ginger in ghee; add to rava.
Mix with curd, salt, chopped coriander and grated carrot. Add water if needed for thick batter consistency. Rest 15–20 minutes.
Just before steaming, add Eno/soda and mix. Pour into greased idli moulds.
Steam 12–15 minutes. Serve with coconut chutney and sambar.
tips: Invented by MTR in Bengaluru during wartime rice shortage.
No fermentation needed – quick and fluffy.

title: Jolada Rotti
recipe: Boil water with salt. Add jowar flour and mix vigorously to form a soft dough. Knead while still warm.
Divide into balls. Pat or roll carefully into thin discs (use wet hands or between sheets).
Cook on a hot tawa on both sides, then finish on open flame for puffing if possible.
Serve with ennegayi (stuffed brinjal), shenga chutney, yogurt or any spicy curry.
tips: Staple of North Karnataka.
Best eaten fresh; dough should be soft and pliable.

title: Kodubale

ingredients.name: Butter or oil, sesame, chilli powder, cumin, salt

recipe: Mix rice flour, roasted gram flour, chilli powder, cumin, sesame, salt and melted butter/oil.
Add hot water to form a stiff dough.
Pinch small portions and shape into rings (kodubale shape).
Deep-fry on medium heat till crisp and golden.
Cool and store in airtight containers.
tips: A classic crunchy tea-time and festive snack.
Shape evenly for uniform frying.

title: Coastal Karnataka Fish Curry

ingredients.name: Tamarind, red chillies, coriander seeds, turmeric

recipe: Grind coconut with roasted red chillies, coriander and a little water to a smooth paste.
Extract tamarind pulp.
In a pot heat oil, sauté onion, garlic and curry leaves. Add the coconut paste, tamarind, turmeric and salt. Bring to a boil.
Gently add fish pieces and simmer on low heat till cooked (do not over-stir).
Serve with rice or neer dosa.
tips: Coastal (Karavali) style uses coconut and local souring agents.
Fresh fish yields the best result.
